topStories.headline: Midlothian Council Greenlights Airport Hangar Design Contract and Digital Ranch Development Deal
topStories.dek: The September 22 City Council meeting advanced two significant economic development items: engineering work for new box hangars at Mid-Way Regional Airport and a development agreement with Digital Ranch LLC tied to a nearly 400-acre rezoning.
topStories.body:
At its regular meeting on Tuesday, September 22, 2026, the Midlothian City Council took up a packed agenda that included two high-profile economic development votes. Under item 2026-332, the council considered and acted upon a Professional Services Agreement with KSA Engineers, Inc. in the amount of $143,235 for design and bidding services for a proposed Box Hangar Development at Mid-Way Regional Airport — a joint facility operated by the cities of Midlothian and Waxahachie on Airport Drive.

Separately, the council considered item 2026-327, authorizing the City Manager to negotiate and enter into a Development Agreement between the City of Midlothian and Digital Ranch LLC. That item was paired with a public hearing (item 2026-326) to rezone approximately 395.7 acres from Agricultural District to a new designation, according to the agenda packet posted on the city's website.

The council also approved a Special Event Permit for a Midlothian High School Alumni Association Homecoming Parade scheduled for Wednesday, October 7, 2026, and authorized a Special Event Permit for a Creekside Manor Haunted House operating on Fridays and Saturdays from October 2 through October 31, 2026.

The September 22 meeting ran approximately two hours and fifteen minutes, according to the city's video archive. The next regular council meeting is scheduled for Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers at City Hall, 215 N. 8th Street.
topStories.sourceName: City of Midlothian — September 22, 2026 Council Agenda Packet

topStories.headline: Monday Is the Last Day to Register to Vote in Ellis County's November 3 Election
topStories.dek: Texas law sets October 5 as the hard deadline to register — or update an existing registration — for the November 3 General and Special Elections, which include the gubernatorial race and county offices.
topStories.body:
Residents of Midlothian, Red Oak, Ovilla, Oak Leaf, and Pecan Hill who are not yet registered to vote have until Monday, October 5, 2026, to do so. The Texas Secretary of State's office confirmed that October 5 is the statewide deadline to register for the November 3, 2026 General Election — 30 days before Election Day as required by Texas law. The deadline applies to new registrations as well as to changes of address or name.

Ellis County's elections page lists the same date and notes that the November 3 ballot will include the gubernatorial election along with other general and special races. Early voting in Ellis County runs from Monday, October 19 through Friday, October 30, 2026. A full list of vote-center polling locations for both early voting and Election Day is posted at elliscountytx.gov/629/Upcoming-Elections.

Texans can check their current registration status, find a registration application, or update their information at VoteTexas.gov. Applications mailed in must be postmarked on or before October 5.

topStories.headline: Ellis County Burn Ban Remains in Effect; Dry Conditions Persist Across the Area
topStories.dek: The Ellis County Commissioners' Court voted in July to impose a countywide burn ban that remains posted as active on official county websites, covering all unincorporated areas including Oak Leaf and Pecan Hill.
topStories.body:
The Ellis County Commissioners' Court voted in favor of a county-wide burn ban at its regular meeting on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, and as of this week the ban remains listed as active on the Ellis County website and the Village of Oak Leaf's official site. The ban covers all unincorporated areas of Ellis County, which includes Oak Leaf and Pecan Hill, and prohibits outdoor burning of brush piles, trash, campfires, and any other open burning.

County officials and the Oak Leaf posting urge residents not to burn anything until the ban is officially lifted, citing dry conditions and the risk that even a small spark can become a dangerous wildfire. Ellis County's website carries the notice under its Emergency Alert section with an 'Effective Immediately' heading.

Residents should check elliscountytx.gov/573/Burn-Ban for the latest status before conducting any outdoor burning. Questions can be directed to the Ellis County Fire Chief.

moreNews.headline: Compass Datacenters' $15M Ellis County Animal Shelter Grant Approved; 830-Acre Red Oak Campus Also Moves Forward
moreNews.body: The Ellis County Commissioners' Court approved a $15 million grant from Compass Datacenters to fund construction of a new municipal animal shelter — a pledge made in a June 2, 2026 announcement following the April 2025 closure of the SPCA of Texas's Ellis County regional care center. The Red Oak-based data center developer had separately received Red Oak City Council approval in May 2026 for a new 830-acre campus, a project that drew a petition signed by more than 2,200 residents. Compass has operated a campus in Red Oak since 2019 and also donated a 40,000-square-foot facility in Red Oak to Texas State Technical College for data center workforce training. Groundbreaking timelines for the animal shelter had not been announced as of the July 2026 KERA News report.

moreNews.headline: Voter Registration Closes Monday, October 5 — Early Voting Begins October 19
moreNews.body: The Texas Secretary of State's office confirmed that Monday, October 5, 2026, is the last day for Ellis County residents to register to vote — or update an existing registration — for the November 3 General and Special Elections. Early voting at Ellis County vote centers runs October 19–30. The full list of polling locations and sample ballots is available at elliscountytx.gov/629/Upcoming-Elections.
